lead: Two labs test the same engine and report two different powers because their procedures differ. A test standard fixes the procedure: what is fitted to the engine, the running-in, the speed, the air conditions and the correction to a reference. The in-cylinder pressure record is the other half: imep, peak pressure, heat release and cycle-to-cycle variation are all derived from it.
prereq: You need: imep and indicated power from the chapter on measuring indicated, brake and friction power, the test cell from the chapter on dynamometers, and the stages of combustion (see Stages of combustion and flame propagation in SI engines).

sections.h3: A rated power is a procedure, not a property

blocks.text: The same engine can be sold as 60 kW or 52 kW. The difference is what was bolted on during the test. A fan, an alternator, an air cleaner and a full exhaust system each take power that the bare engine never sees.

items: Gross power: bare engine, only the pumps needed for its own operation, no fan, no alternator, no silencer.
Net power: with the production fan, alternator, air cleaner and exhaust system fitted, as installed in the vehicle.
Running-in: the standard fixes how long the engine runs before measurement, and at what load.
Steady state: power is quoted at a fixed speed, with coolant and oil at declared temperatures, after readings stop drifting.

blocks.text: ISO 1585 covers net power of automotive engines. ISO 3046 covers power ratings of reciprocating engines for industrial and marine use with continuous and overload ratings. SAE J1349 is the American net-power procedure. Stationary engines in India are tested to IS 10000, the Indian standard methods of test for internal combustion engines. Quote the convention, the speed and the fuel along with the power, or the number means nothing.

sections.h3: Reference air and the driving cycle

blocks.text: Air density decides how much fuel can be burnt, so a cold January morning in Delhi and a hot May afternoon give different power from the same engine. Standards correct measured power to reference air, 25 °C and 99 kPa dry air pressure, by multiplying the measured value by a correction factor.

α is the correction factor for a spark-ignition engine in ISO 1585; p<sub>d</sub> is the dry air pressure at the inlet in kPa (barometric minus vapour pressure); T is the inlet air temperature in K; 99 kPa and 298 K are the reference values. Corrected power P₀ = α × P. Diesel engines use other exponents. The formula is used only while α stays between 0.93 and 1.07.

items: NEDC: 1180 s, about 11.0 km, two phases (urban, extra-urban), gentle accelerations.
WLTC: 1800 s, about 23.3 km, four phases, higher speeds and harder accelerations.
MIDC: the modified Indian driving cycle, adapted for Indian road speeds; it is the type-approval cycle for BS VI cars and light-duty vehicles, while two-wheelers are certified on WMTC.
BS VI: the current Indian stage, with separate petrol and diesel limits in g/km; for a petrol car, CO is capped near 1.0 g/km and NOx near 0.06 g/km.

blocks.text: The cycle sets the speed and load history, so the cycle decides the number. A CO figure from NEDC cannot be compared with a CO figure from WLTC.

In a spark-ignition engine the cylinder pressure swings from about 1 bar to 80 bar within 40° of crank angle, thousands of times a minute; in a turbocharged diesel the peak can reach about 150 bar or more. The chain that records it has four jobs: sense, convert, time-stamp, store.

items: Transducer: a piezoelectric quartz crystal with its diaphragm flush with the combustion chamber wall, so no passage fills with carbon; hot engines use a water-cooled body.

Charge to voltage: the crystal releases a small charge, of the order of picocoulombs per bar; a charge amplifier turns it into a voltage proportional to pressure. Cable movement and moisture also make charge, so low-noise cable is used.
Crank-angle timing: an encoder on the crankshaft gives one pulse per degree plus an index pulse once per revolution.
Logging: the data acquisition system samples pressure at every encoder pulse for 100 or more consecutive cycles and stores each sample against its crank angle.

TDC reference and pegging: the encoder index is tied to true TDC with a TDC sensor or a motoring run. The relative piezo record is then shifted by one constant, either so that the pressure near bottom dead centre of the intake stroke equals the intake manifold pressure, or so that the compression line follows pVn = constant. That gives absolute pressure.

blocks.text: Without pegging the trace floats at the wrong absolute level: peak pressure and the heat-release curve come out wrong, but the imep taken as the closed-cycle integral ∮p dV is largely unaffected, because a constant offset cancels in the integral. A TDC (angle) error does change imep, because every pressure is paired with the wrong volume; this is why TDC is located carefully.

items: p-θ plot: peak pressure and the crank angle where it occurs; the slope gives the maximum rate of pressure rise.
p-V plot: the enclosed area of the closed cycle is indicated work; divide by displacement per cycle to get imep. A log p versus log V plot gives the polytropic index.
Heat release rate: from the first law applied to the cylinder contents, using p-θ and V-θ; the crank angles for 10 % and 90 % burnt define the combustion duration.
Cycle-to-cycle variation: compute imep for each cycle separately and take the coefficient of variation.

blocks.where: σ is the standard deviation of imep over the recorded cycles (bar); μ is the mean imep (bar); COV is the coefficient of variation in percent. Below about 5 % is taken as stable combustion; a highly diluted engine that drifts past it is close to misfire.

examples.question: A piezoelectric transducer and a crank-angle encoder record 100 cycles of a 1.5 L four-stroke engine running at 2000 rpm. Mean imep over the 100 cycles is 8.2 bar, with a standard deviation of 0.21 bar; peak pressure is 62 bar at 14° ATDC. Find the indicated power and the coefficient of variation of imep. Is the combustion stable?
steps: Convert imep to SI: 8.2 bar = 8.2 × 10⁵ Pa.
A four-stroke engine fires once per two revolutions, so cycles per second = N/120 = 2000/120 = 16.67 s⁻¹.
Indicated power IP = imep × V<sub>d</sub> × (N/120) = 8.2 × 10⁵ × 1.5 × 10⁻³ × 16.67 = 20 500 W = 20.5 kW.
The usual limit for stable combustion is 5 %, so 2.56 % is well inside it.
examples.answer: Indicated power is 20.5 kW and the COV of imep is 2.56 %, so combustion is stable.
examples.check:
imep = 8.2e5
vd = 1.5e-3
n = 2000
cyc = n / 120
ip = imep * vd * cyc
print(round(ip, 1))
print(round(ip / 1000, 1))
cov = 0.21 / 8.2 * 100
print(round(cov, 2))

examples.question: A petrol engine gives 52.0 kW on a day when the inlet air is at 35 °C and the dry air pressure is 96.0 kPa. Find its corrected power by the spark-ignition formula.
steps: α = 1.0376 × 1.0200 = 1.0584, inside 0.93 to 1.07, so the formula may be used.
examples.answer: α = 1.058 and the corrected power is 55.0 kW, about 6 % above the observed 52.0 kW.

traps: Using the piezo signal as absolute pressure. It is relative until pegged: an unpegged trace gives wrong peak pressure and heat release, although the loop area (imep) hardly changes.
Comparing a gross rating with a net rating, or an NEDC emission figure with a WLTC one. Different procedures, different numbers.
Forgetting the factor 2 for a four-stroke: using N/60 instead of N/120 in the imep-to-power step doubles the answer.
Ignoring TDC offset. A one-degree error shifts the peak-pressure angle and changes imep and heat release, because each pressure is paired with the wrong volume.
Quoting COV as a fraction when the question asks for a percentage, or computing COV of peak pressure while calling it COV of imep.

quiz.q: State the difference between gross and net rated power.
quiz.a: Gross power is measured on a bare engine with only the pumps needed for its own operation. Net power is measured with the production fan, alternator, air cleaner and exhaust system fitted.

quiz.q: Why does a piezoelectric pressure signal need pegging?
quiz.a: The charge leaks away slowly, so the crystal gives pressure changes, not absolute pressure. Pegging shifts the whole record by one constant, for example so that the pressure at intake bottom dead centre equals the intake manifold pressure, or so that the compression line follows pV<sup>n</sup> = constant.

quiz.q: A four-stroke engine of 2.0 L displacement has imep 9 bar at 3000 rpm. Find the indicated power.
quiz.a: imep = 9 × 10⁵ Pa, V<sub>d</sub> = 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³, cycles per second = 3000/120 = 25. IP = 9 × 10⁵ × 2.0 × 10⁻³ × 25 = 45 000 W = 45 kW.

quiz.q: Over 100 cycles the mean imep is 7.5 bar with a standard deviation of 0.30 bar. Find the COV.
quiz.a: COV = (0.30/7.5) × 100 = 4.0 %, just inside the 5 % stability limit.

quiz.q: COV of imep rises from 2 % at stoichiometric to 7 % at a very lean mixture. What does that tell you about the engine?
quiz.a: The lean mixture burns slowly and the flame may not establish every cycle, so imep scatters cycle by cycle. A COV above 5 % means partial misfires and rising unburnt hydrocarbon emissions, so that lean limit is not usable without charge stratification or faster combustion.

quiz.q: Why can an emission figure from NEDC not be compared with one from WLTC?
quiz.a: Each cycle is a different speed and load trace, with different accelerations, top speeds and durations. The engine's temperature history and transient fuelling differ, so the measured g/km belongs to that cycle only.

quiz.q: A 1° error in TDC reference is suspected. Which measured quantities move, and why?
quiz.a: Peak pressure angle moves, because the whole p-θ curve is shifted against the volume; imep changes because each pressure is paired with the wrong volume; heat release rate changes most, because it depends on dp/dθ and dV/dθ at the same angle.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern test cells use cylinder pressure in real time, trimming injection or spark cycle by cycle from imep and the 50 % burnt angle. Standards are moving toward real-driving and in-service testing with portable measurement. Search next for cylinder pressure pegging and portable emission measurement systems.
